overview: A media caption component that pairs an image with descriptive label text. Use it to provide context, attribution, or supplementary information beneath figures, photos, and illustrations.

whenToUse: Beneath a figure, photo, or illustration to attribute the source or provide supplementary context
When an image needs a short descriptive label that clarifies its subject or origin for the reader
do: Keep caption text concise — one or two short sentences at most
Use the label (bold) portion for the attribution or primary identifier, and the description for supporting detail
Use left alignment when the caption sits beneath a left-aligned or full-bleed image in a text-heavy layout
Use the italics style for editorial or journalistic contexts where captions are conventionally set in italic
dont: Don't use a caption as a substitute for meaningful alt text — the two serve different purposes and both are needed
Don't repeat the surrounding body copy verbatim in the caption; add value with attribution or additional context
Don't use all-caps style for long captions — it reduces legibility and should be reserved for very short labels or identifiers
